title: POC scoping: Benchmark planning & harness integration
summary: Redwood and Nimbus aligned on POC success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput targets, quality baselines). Discussed harness integration: customer will provide existing Locust scripts and sample traffic traces; Redwood to provide benchmark runbook, example config for streaming and non-streaming, and initial cluster sizing. Key decisions: run both streaming and non-streaming tests, include KV cache warm-up, measure p90/p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens. Timeline: initial harness handoff 11/05, first run 11/12, results review 11/16.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-02 08:45 PST, duration ~54m. Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we wanted to go through the POC scope and specifically the benchmarking and harness integration portion — make sure we can reproduce your traffic and capture both streaming and non-stream behavior.
[00:22] Sarah Kim: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we run a patient triage microservice that calls LLM for summarization and follow-up question generation. Typical response size is ~180-350 tokens, about 60% streaming in prod. We're using a mix of synchronous calls and some server-side streaming to UX.
[00:45] Jonas Reed: Got it. Can you share current TPS and concurrency numbers? That will drive sizing for the harness.
[00:51] Liam O'Connor: Sure, average steady TPS is 12, spike to 120 TPS during morning syncs, about 300 concurrent active requests at peak. Latency SLO is p95 < 400ms for generation-only calls, p95 < 600ms for calls that do a two-step (embedding + generation).
[01:18] Maya Patel: Perfect, that gives us targets. For the POC success criteria we usually recommend: 1) Meet customer p95 SLO for the targeted workload, 2) provide unit economics (cost per 1M tokens) within agreed bounds, 3) consistent behavior for streaming vs non-streaming, and 4) no stability regressions across a 6-hour soak run. Any additions?
[01:40] Ethan Miller: Include quality baseline — we have evaluation prompts, we'll need accuracy/ROUGE-ish checks to ensure model variants don't regress. Also security: all data must be in our VPC for private POC.
[02:01] Carlos Vega: Noted on VPC. For the harness integration — what do you currently use? Locust? JMeter? Custom k6?
[02:12] Priya Desai: We have a custom Python load harness built on top of Locust and a collection of real request traces saved as ndjson. We can export per-request token counts and latencies.
[02:28] Jonas Reed: That's ideal. If you can hand over a sample of the Locust scripts and a sanitized traffic trace (say 1k requests) we can create a mapping to Redwood's API and provide a runbook.
[02:39] Sarah Kim: We'll sanitize and share by 11/05. 
[02:45] Maya Patel: Great. Two paths for testing streaming: 1) emulate streaming at the client level with chunked response handling in the harness, or 2) run non-streaming tests where the model returns the full text and we measure end-to-end latency. We'll run both. Any preference for which to prioritize?
[03:06] Liam O'Connor: We care more about streaming since that's 60% of production, but we also want the non-streaming numbers for cost comparison.
[03:16] Maya Patel: Okay we'll prioritize streaming. For streaming tests we need the harness to wait for incremental tokens and capture per-chunk latency as well as total time-to-first-byte and time-to-last-byte.
[03:30] Priya Desai: Our scripts already capture chunk-level timestamps, should be straightforward.
[03:36] Jonas Reed: Great. On the Redwood side we'll provide two configs: a streaming-optimized route and a non-streaming route. We'll also include a config for quantized model variants if you want to test lower-cost options.
[03:50] Sarah Kim: Yes please include 8-bit/4-bit quantized runs but mark them as sanity only; we want to verify quality.
[03:58] Maya Patel: For workload sizing — based on the numbers you provided, we'd recommend starting the benchmark cluster with 4x A10s (or equivalent) for dedicated test, with autoscale to 8 during spikes. That's to hit the 120 TPS spikes while keeping p95 under 400ms; we'll refine after initial run.
[04:22] Ethan Miller: A10s are fine. What's the expected cost for the pilot run?
[04:28] Carlos Vega: We'll provide an estimate in the runbook — but ballpark for 48h of benchmarking with that cluster is included in benchmark cost sheet we'll share.
[04:36] Sarah Kim: Also, do you do KV cache warm-up? We rely heavily on prefix caching for multi-turn.
[04:42] Jonas Reed: Yes, we'll include a warm-up phase in the harness — replaying recent sessions to populate KV cache before measurement windows. We'll document warm-up length (we typically do 30–60 minutes depending on recurrence).
[04:58] Priya Desai: Our average conversation depth is 4 turns, token reuse is high, so warm-up will matter.
[05:06] Maya Patel: Good note. For success criteria we want to capture a small matrix: latency (p50/p90/p95), throughput (TPS), token cost (USD / 1M tokens), and quality (your eval prompts pass threshold). We'll include stability checks and memory/GC warnings from runtime logs.
[05:24] Liam O'Connor: On observability, can Redwood capture per-request trace IDs and forward logs to our splunk or datadog?
[05:31] Carlos Vega: We can stream traces and metrics to your Datadog via an export, and include trace IDs in response headers for correlation. We'll include instructions in the runbook.
[05:42] Sarah Kim: Great.
[05:46] Maya Patel: Let's walk through what we'll need from Nimbus to integrate the harness: 1) sample Locust scripts, 2) 1k sanitized ndjson traces, 3) evaluation prompt set and baseline scores, 4) expected SLO matrix and acceptable cost ceiling, and 5) example VPC peering info for networking test. Anything else?
[06:11] Sarah Kim: I'll add the encryption/KMS requirements — we need to use our KMS with Bring Your Own Key for Private deployment tests.
[06:20] Jonas Reed: That matters mainly for Private mode; for hosted POC we can encrypt at rest but for BYOK we'll schedule a security review.
[06:30] Ethan Miller: Security review needs to be completed before any production-like runs. Timeline?
[06:34] Maya Patel: We'll aim to finish the security/Q&A by 11/10; you said you'll share docs 11/05 so that gives a 5 day window.
[06:43] Priya Desai: Sounds good.
[06:46] Maya Patel: Next — benchmark scenarios and metrics. We'll run: baseline (cold start, no cache), warm-up (KV cache populated), steady-state 1hr at average TPS, spike test (ramp to 120TPS), soak 6hr at 20–30TPS to test stability, and streaming-specific runs capturing chunk timings.
[07:09] Sarah Kim: For spike test, can we push to 150TPS for a short burst? That's occasionally observed on real traffic.
[07:14] Jonas Reed: We can do a short 5-minute 150TPS burst but we'll note degradation points and fallback behavior.
[07:21] Maya Patel: We'll also include model fallback scenarios — test what happens when primary model is slow and Redwood routes to a lower-cost variant. We'll capture quality delta during fallback.
[07:34] Priya Desai: Important for us — fallback mustn't change the response schema.
[07:39] Carlos Vega: We'll ensure function outputs remain consistent; will add a schema-check step in harness.
[07:44] Sarah Kim: How do you handle streaming vs non-streaming in terms of cost accounting?
[07:50] Maya Patel: We report tokens and compute separately — streaming has slightly higher per-request overhead but better perceived latency. We'll provide cost per token and per-request overhead in the results.
[07:59] Liam O'Connor: For the harness execution environment — do you prefer Redwood to run in your cluster pointed at our VPC, or do you want us to run harness against Redwood-hosted endpoints?
[08:11] Maya Patel: Either works. For security and network realism, best is to run from your side inside the VPC peered to Redwood test cluster. But if you prefer less setup, we can run from our bench cluster and share raw traffic traces and results.
[08:27] Ethan Miller: We'll run from our VPC.
[08:30] Maya Patel: Good. We'll provide an infrastructure-as-code snippet to create the test harness worker instances and the peering steps.
[08:38] Priya Desai: Scripting details — our Locust uses websockets for streaming; can Redwood accept a websocket-based streaming test, or do you emulate with chunked HTTP?
[08:48] Jonas Reed: We support both; for fidelity, websocket-based harness is best. We'll provide a small Python example that wraps Locust events to the Redwood streaming API.
[08:59] Sarah Kim: Excellent.
[09:02] Maya Patel: On the metrics side we'll export Prometheus metrics and a summary CSV with per-request timings and token counts. Please confirm which fields you want in the CSV.
[09:14] Priya Desai: Minimal fields: request_id, start_ts, first_chunk_ts, last_chunk_ts, request_tokens, response_tokens, p50/p90/p95 windows, error_flag, model_variant.
[09:30] Carlos Vega: We'll include those.
[09:33] Maya Patel: Now timelines and milestones: 11/05 — Nimbus shares scripts and traces; 11/06 — Redwood provide runbook, IaC snippet, and initial sizing; 11/12 — first benchmark runs (streaming + non-streaming); 11/13 — internal analysis; 11/16 — joint results review and decision on next steps. Any conflicts?
[09:55] Liam O'Connor: We can meet that. Security doc turnaround might vary but we'll try.
[09:59] Sarah Kim: One more question — what about model variants and quantization matrix?
[10:05] Jonas Reed: We'll propose three variants: full fp16 baseline, 8-bit quantized, and 4-bit aggressive quant. We'll run quality checks and label each run.
[10:16] Maya Patel: Also, we'll surface memory/oom events and any runtime retries. If you have known reproducible traces for rare failure modes, share them.
[10:25] Priya Desai: We do; will include a couple error traces.
[10:29] Maya Patel: Ok, moving to action items recap.
[10:33] Maya Patel: Action items — Maya to send runbook and pricing sheet; Jonas to prepare streaming example and IaC; Nimbus to send scripts and traces by 11/05; Carlos to schedule security review invite; team to run initial bench 11/12.
[10:50] Sarah Kim: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[10:53] Ethan Miller: Quick note — include a column for tokenized prompt size in the CSV, that impacts cost calc.
[10:58] Jonas Reed: Will do.
[11:01] Maya Patel: Any final questions?
[11:03] Sarah Kim: No, good plan.
[11:05] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the runbook and calendar invites.

[53:30] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'A10s' could be transcribed as 'A tens'), filler words retained, speaker attributions sometimes generalized.
